references.text: Jesus says that everything the Father has is his – the same thought as the father's words "all that is mine is yours" ([ref:Joh 16:15|John 16:15]).
In Jesus' high priestly prayer, the same fellowship between the Father and the Son is expressed: "All that is mine is yours, and what is yours is mine" ([ref:Joh 17:10|John 17:10]).
Paul writes that believers are God's heirs and co-heirs with Christ, which reflects the father's words that everything he has belongs to his son ([ref:Rom 8:17|Romans 8:17]).
Jesus emphasizes his unbreakable fellowship with the Father – knowing the Son is knowing the Father – paralleling the father's assurance "you are always with me" ([ref:Joh 14:9-11|John 14:9-11]).
The context of the parable: the Pharisees and the scribes grumbled because Jesus welcomed sinners, and the older son represents this attitude ([ref:Luk 15:2|Luke 15:2]).
Paul reminds us that "all things are yours" – a thought similar to the father's words to his son that everything he has belongs to him ([ref:1 Kor 3:21-23|1 Corinthians 3:21-23]).

The psalmist confesses: "I am always with you" – an expression of the close fellowship with God, which is reflected in the father's words "you are always with me" ([ref:Sal 73:23-25|Psalms 73:23-25]).

The law of the birthright, where the firstborn son receives a double portion, forms the background for the older son's position and the father's assurance that everything he has belongs to his son ([ref:5 Mos 21:17|Deuteronomy 21:17]).
